questions.question: Bihu festival is the main festival of which state?
questions.solution:
Bihu is the most significant festival of Assam, celebrated three times a year to mark different stages of the agricultural cycle: Rongali Bihu (Spring/New Year), Kati Bihu (Autumn), and Magh Bihu (Harvest).

Note: It is a secular festival celebrated by all Assamese people regardless of caste or religion.

questions.question: Hola Mohalla is a festival associated with which religion/belief?
questions.solution:
Hola Mohalla is a Sikh festival usually celebrated a day after Holi. Established by Guru Gobind Singh Ji, it is a grand event that showcases martial arts, simulated battles (Gatka), and military exercises.

Location: The primary celebrations take place at Anandpur Sahib in Punjab.

questions.question: The ‘Lokranjan’ festival celebrates the folk and tribal culture of which Indian state?
questions.solution:
The Lokranjan festival is a national folk dance festival organized annually by the Madhya Pradesh Tourism Development Corporation in Khajuraho, Madhya Pradesh.

Objective: It serves as a platform to showcase the diverse folk and tribal cultures of various Indian states through dance and music.

questions.question: Rottela Panduga or the Roti Festival is celebrated in which Indian state?
questions.solution:
Rottela Panduga (Festival of Breads) is a unique three-day annual festival held at the Bara Shaheed Dargah in Nellore, Andhra Pradesh.

Tradition: Devotees exchange rotis (flatbreads) in the Swarnala Cheruvu tank as a way of seeking blessings or thanking for fulfilled wishes.

questions.question: Vishu festival is celebrated in which of the following states?
questions.solution:
Vishu is the Malayalam New Year celebrated primarily in Kerala and parts of Karnataka (Tulunadu) and Tamil Nadu.

Ritual: The most important part is the Vishukkani, the first thing one sees upon waking up, which includes auspicious items like yellow flowers (Konna), fruits, and gold.

questions.question: Which of the following celebrations is dedicated to Sun God and his wife Usha to thank them for sustaining life on earth and for granting wishes?
questions.solution:
Chhath Puja is an ancient Vedic festival dedicated to the Sun God (Surya) and Chhathi Maiya (Usha). It is observed to thank them for supporting life on earth.

Practice: It involves rigorous rituals including fasting and standing in water to offer 'Arghya' during sunset and sunrise.

questions.question: ‘Nuakhai’ is the state festival of:
questions.solution:
Nuakhai is an agricultural festival primarily celebrated in Odisha (especially Western Odisha) to welcome the new harvest of the season.

Etymology: 'Nua' means new and 'Khai' means food. The first grains of the harvest are offered to the presiding deities like Goddess Samaleswari.

questions.question: Which of the following festivals is celebrated as the birth anniversary of Guru Nanak Dev?
questions.solution:
Gurpurab (specifically Guru Nanak Gurpurab) marks the birth anniversary of Guru Nanak Dev Ji, the founder of Sikhism. It is one of the most sacred festivals in Sikhism.

Celebration: It involves Akhand Path (continuous reading of Guru Granth Sahib), processions (Nagarkirtan), and community kitchens (Langar).

questions.question: Harela is a festival of greenery, peace, prosperity, and environmental conservation, primarily celebrated in which of the following states?
questions.solution:
Harela is a festival of greenery and prosperity celebrated in the Kumaon region of Uttarakhand. It marks the beginning of the rainy season and the Shravan month.

Note: On this day, people plant saplings to promote environmental conservation and pray for a good harvest.

questions.question: ‘Sangken’ is a festival celebrated in Arunachal Pradesh by people of which of the following religions?
questions.solution:
Sangken is the traditional New Year festival of the Buddhist communities in Arunachal Pradesh (like the Khampti and Singpho tribes).

Theme: It is a water festival similar to Songkran in Thailand, where people sprinkle water on Buddha idols and each other as a symbol of purification.

questions.question: ’Poush Mela’ is a unique festival celebrated in which of the following Indian states?
questions.solution:
Poush Mela is an annual fair and festival held in Santiniketan, West Bengal. It marks the foundation day of Brahmo Samaj and celebrates the harvest season.

Features: The fair is famous for live performances of Baul music, folk dances, and local handicrafts.

questions.question: In which state/UT is the Hemis festival celebrated?
questions.solution:
The Hemis Festival is celebrated in Ladakh at the Hemis Gompa (monastery) to honor the birth of Guru Padmasambhava.

Highlight: The festival is world-renowned for its Cham Dance, a colorful masked dance performed by monks representing the victory of good over evil.

questions.question: Gangaur Festival, Pushkar Fair, Nagaur Fair and Urs Fair are the popular fairs and festivals of which state?
questions.solution: Rajasthan is famous for its vibrant fairs and festivals like Gangaur (celebrated by women), the Pushkar Fair (the world's largest camel fair), the Nagaur Fair, and the Urs of Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti in Ajmer.

questions.question: Thrissur Pooram is one of the famous temple festivals celebrated in _______.
questions.solution:
Thrissur Pooram is the most famous temple festival of Kerala, held at the Vadakkunnathan Temple.

Spectacle: It is known for its magnificent display of decorated elephants (Gajmela), competitive exchange of colorful umbrellas (Kudamattam), and spectacular fireworks.

questions.question: Chhath Puja is the main festival of which state?
questions.solution:
Chhath Puja is the most important cultural and religious festival of Bihar. While also celebrated in Jharkhand and UP, it is the defining festival of the Bihari diaspora.

Note: It is unique because it is one of the few Hindu festivals where there is no idol worship.

questions.question: The festival of ‘Rath Yatra’ of Puri in Odisha is dedicated to which deity?
questions.solution:
The Rath Yatra (Chariot Festival) in Puri, Odisha, is dedicated to Lord Jagannath (a form of Krishna).

Event: It involves the journey of the deities from the main temple to the Gundicha Temple in three massive wooden chariots pulled by thousands of devotees.

questions.question: Paryushana festival is celebrated by the people of which of the following communities?
questions.solution:
Paryushana is the most important annual holy event for the Jain community. It is a period of intensive fasting, repentance, and spiritual reflection.

Key Concept: It concludes with Kshamavani, a day where Jains seek forgiveness from all living beings for any harm caused.

questions.question: Chariot festival is dedicated to Lord Jagannath along with Subhadra and _________ .
questions.solution:
The Chariot Festival (Rath Yatra) features three deities: Lord Jagannath, his sister Subhadra, and his elder brother Balabhadra (also known as Balarama).

Fact: Each deity has their own specific chariot; Jagannath's chariot is called Nandighosha.

questions.question: Navratri festival is dedicated to which of the following Goddesses?
questions.solution:
Navratri is a nine-night festival dedicated to Goddess Durga and her nine avatars (Navadurga).

Regional Variation: In the North, it involves Ramlila; in the West, Garba; and in the East, it is celebrated as Durga Puja.

questions.question: Easter festival is celebrated by which community?
questions.solution:
Easter is a Christian festival celebrating the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead.

Timing: It is observed on the first Sunday after the full moon following the spring equinox. It symbolizes hope, renewal, and the triumph of life over death.

questions.question: In which of the following states is Me-dam-me-phi festival primarily celebrated?
questions.solution:
Me-Dam-Me-Phi is the most important ancestor-worship festival of the Ahom community in Assam.

Meaning: 'Me' means offerings, 'Dam' means ancestors, and 'Phi' means gods. It is celebrated every year on January 31st.

questions.question: ‘Atla Taddi’ is the widely celebrated festival of which Indian state?
questions.solution:
Atla Taddi is a traditional festival celebrated by married Hindu women in Andhra Pradesh for the health and long life of their husbands.

Comparison: It is often compared to the Karwa Chauth festival celebrated in North India.

questions.question: Which of the following is a festival primarily celebrated in the state of Odisha?
questions.solution:
Raja Parba is a unique three-day festival in Odisha that celebrates womanhood and the Earth's menstruation.

Tradition: It is believed that the Mother Earth prepares for the agricultural season during these days; people refrain from walking barefoot on the soil and enjoy swings (Doli).

questions.question: By what name is the festival of Makar Sankranti celebrated in Assam?
questions.solution:
In Assam, Makar Sankranti is celebrated as Magh Bihu (also called Bhogali Bihu).

Activities: It is a harvest festival characterized by community feasts and the burning of temporary bamboo huts called Mejis.

questions.question: Which of the following festivals observed in Assam is majorly celebrated by Vaishnavites?
questions.solution:
Doljatra (or Dola Purnima) is a major festival in Assam and West Bengal, predominantly celebrated by Vaishnavites (followers of Lord Vishnu/Krishna).

Connection: It celebrates the divine love of Radha and Krishna and coincides with the festival of Holi.

questions.question: Makar Sankranti is the festival dedicated to which of the following Lords?
questions.solution: Makar Sankranti is a solar festival dedicated to the Sun God (Surya). It marks the transition of the Sun into the zodiac sign of Capricorn (Makara) and the beginning of the Uttarayan (northward movement).

questions.question: The birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi is celebrated as the national festival of India. In which of the following years was Gandhi ji born?
questions.solution:
Mahatma Gandhi was born on October 2, 1869, in Porbandar, Gujarat.

Significance: His birthday is celebrated as Gandhi Jayanti in India and the International Day of Non-Violence worldwide.

questions.question: Sardhana Christian Fair is held in which of the following states?
questions.solution:
The Sardhana Christian Fair is held at the Basilica of Our Lady of Graces in Sardhana, Uttar Pradesh.

Historical Context: Sardhana was the capital of Begum Samru, who built this magnificent church in the 19th century.

questions.question: Kajari Mahotsav is primarily celebrated in which of the following districts of Uttar Pradesh?
questions.solution:
Kajari Mahotsav is a prominent cultural festival celebrated in Mirzapur, Uttar Pradesh.

Music: It is centered around Kajari, a genre of folk song traditionally sung during the rainy season, often expressing the longing of a woman for her lover.

questions.question: Lathmar Holi is primarily celebrated in the state of:
questions.solution:
Lathmar Holi is a world-famous tradition celebrated in Barsana and Nandgaon near Mathura in Uttar Pradesh.

Ritual: In this unique celebration, women playfully beat men with sticks (lathis) while the men protect themselves with shields.

questions.question: Shab-e-Barat is celebrated by which religious group?
questions.solution:
Shab-e-Barat (the Night of Forgiveness) is a significant night celebrated by the Muslim community.

Belief: It is believed that on this night, God determines the fortunes and future of all people for the coming year. It is observed with prayers, fasting, and visiting graves.

questions.question: Kati Bihu is celebrated in which of the following months in Assam?
questions.solution:
Kati Bihu (also known as Kongali Bihu) is celebrated in the month of October in Assam.

Nature: Unlike the other Bihus, it is a solemn occasion. People light lamps (Saki) in front of Tulsi plants and in the paddy fields to pray for a good harvest and protection from pests.

questions.question: In India, Teachers’ Day is celebrated annually on September 5 to mark the birthday of:
questions.solution:
Teachers' Day in India is celebrated on September 5 to honor the birth of Dr. Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan.

Profile: He was a world-renowned philosopher, a great teacher, and the second President of independent India.
